message.content:
This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   - Fix Orchestration page to be fully functional with proper UI/UX and end-to-end flow
   - Add optimization to orchestration (avoid wasted API calls on start nodes)
   - Test global agents and make them easily accessible
   - Fix Global CLAUDE.md's broken agent routing (referenced non-existent agents)
   - Make agents fully available across all Boldteq apps with zero technical setup
   - Set up pm2 as background service + LaunchAgent for auto-start on login
   - Create @boldteq/agents SDK installable in all projects
   - Add Setup & Status page to Claude Hub showing full system health
   - Create documentation folder with comprehensive setup guides
   - Final request (most recent): "make sure there full documentation available where all explain step by step and also make sure all option available in set up to ensure its explain well clear with notes to ensure in future if lost anything we can get all thing"

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - **Claude Code agents** — `.md` files in `~/.claude/agents/` loaded automatically every session
   - **Slash commands** — `.claude/commands/` files invoked by user typing `/commandname` in VS Code
   - **Agent vs slash command distinction** — agents are sub-agents Claude spawns internally; commands are user-invocable
   - **pm2** — Node.js process manager keeping Claude Hub running as background service
   - **LaunchAgent (macOS)** — plist in `~/Library/LaunchAgents/` for auto-start on login
   - **@boldteq/agents SDK** — shared npm package at `claude-hub/sdk/` installable as `file:../claude-hub/sdk`
   - **Server-Sent Events (SSE)** — streaming orchestration execution results from backend to frontend
   - **Topological sort** — Kahn's algorithm for DAG execution order with numbered badges on nodes
   - **ReactFlow** — visual DAG builder for orchestration
   - **Orchestration prompt construction** — fixed to include explicit deliverable directive
   - **CORS** — enabled in Claude Hub for cross-app calls from local projects
   - **ecosystem.config.js** — pm2 configuration file handling paths with spaces

3. Files and Code Sections:

   - **`/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/claude-hub/src/server.js`**
     - Fixed orchestration prompt construction — old: `"Provide your response:"` / new: separates base instructions + node task + context + explicit "Produce the actual deliverable directly. Do NOT write meta-commentary"
     - Added `POST /api/playground/run` — runs any agent via SSE stream
     - Added `GET /api/setup/status` — returns pm2Status, launchAgentInstalled, agentCount, sdkExists, port
     - Added `GET /api/setup/projects` — checks each project for SDK installation
     - Added `POST /api/setup/install-sdk` — installs SDK in a project via npm install

   - **`/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/claude-hub/client/src/pages/Orchestration.tsx`**
     - Added execution order badges (purple numbered circles) via topological sort useMemo
     - Progressive Run button (open panel → run with task)
     - Post-run Re-run/Reset buttons
     - Full output viewer modal triggered by clicking completed nodes or "View full output"
     - processSSEEvent useCallback helper for SSE handling
     - Disconnected node validation before run
     - `deleteKeyCode={["Backspace", "Delete"]}` for Mac
     - "New" button in toolbar, guide modal with help (?) button
     - `nodes={nodesWithOrder}` instead of `nodes={nodes}`

   - **`/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/claude-hub/client/src/pages/Playground.tsx`** (created)
     - Agent selector dropdown with search/filter
     - Test prompt textarea with Cmd+Enter shortcut
     - SSE stream parsing for output display
     - Test history (last 20) with duration tracking, click to reload
     - Re-run, Cancel, Copy buttons

   - **`/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/claude-hub/client/src/pages/Setup.tsx`** (fully rebuilt)
     - 10 sections with comprehensive content
     - StatusCard component with ok/warn/error states and notes
     - NoteBox component for info/warn/tip callouts
     - Collapsible component for expandable sections
     - CodeBlock with copy button
     - System Health (4 cards with fix commands shown when red)
     - Project SDK Status table with one-click Install buttons
     - Global Agent Roster (all 12 agents: file, name, model, use when)
     - Build flow diagram + quick task routing reference
     - SDK usage collapsibles (basic usage, all functions, manual install)
     - Slash commands collapsibles (how they work, Pinzo's commands, agent wrappers)
     - Orchestration quick reference
     - pm2 & LaunchAgent full command reference with Fresh Machine Setup
     - Global CLAUDE.md section
     - Troubleshooting (7 issues with cause + fix + CodeBlock)
     - Docs reference table (8 files)

   - **`~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`** (updated)
     - Replaced broken "Agent Routing" table (had: factory, researcher, stack-shopify) with correct "Agent Roster" table listing all 12 agents with filenames
     - Fixed Stack B: "React Router 7" replacing "Remix"
     - Added explicit routing rules section
     - Updated Active Projects table with real stacks and paths

   - **`/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/claude-hub/sdk/`** (created)
     - `package.json` — name: `@boldteq/agents`, private: true
     - `index.js` — callAgent(), listAgents(), isOnline() as CommonJS exports
     - `index.d.ts` — TypeScript declarations for all exports

   - **`/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/claude-hub/ecosystem.config.js`** (created)
     - pm2 config with cwd set to full path (handles spaces in "Boldteq App")
     - interpreter: 'node', autorestart: true, max_restarts: 5

   - **`/Users/yashbaldha/Library/LaunchAgents/io.boldteq.claude-hub.plist`** (created)
     - Runs node src/server.js on login
     - KeepAlive: true, RunAtLoad: true
     - Points to nvm Node path: `/Users/yashbaldha/.nvm/versions/node/v20.20.1/bin/node`

   - **`/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/claude-hub/docs/`** (created 5 files, background agent writing 8)
     - Currently: 01-setup.md (98 lines), 02-agents.md (76 lines), 03-sdk.md (157 lines), 04-slash-commands.md (103 lines), 05-orchestration.md (43 lines)
     - Background agent writing: 00-overview.md (NEW), full rewrites of 01-07, plus 06-new-project.md and 07-troubleshooting.md (both NEW)

   - **All 6 project `package.json` files** (updated)
     - Added `"@boldteq/agents": "file:../claude-hub/sdk"` to dependencies
     - Confirmed all 6 have sdk=True: Pinzo, Rankora, QuizSnap, Size Chart & Recommender, CROBOT, Store Locator

   - **`client/src/App.tsx`** (updated)
     - Added imports for Playground and Setup
     - Added routes: `/playground` and `/setup`

   - **`client/src/components/Sidebar.tsx`** (updated)
     - Added FlaskConical import → Playground nav link
     - Added Wrench import → Setup & Status nav link under System section

4. Errors and Fixes:
   - **Orchestration TypeScript error**: `nodesWithOrder` type conflict with ReactFlow — Fixed by adding `as Node[]` cast
   - **JSON parsing error in orchestration**: "Unexpected token '<'" — Root cause was old test server still running, not actual code issue
   - **pm2 path with spaces**: pm2 couldn't handle `/Boldteq App/` path directly — Fixed by creating ecosystem.config.js with `cwd` set to full path
   - **pm2 EADDRINUSE on restart**: Port 3847 held by old test process — Fixed with `lsof -ti:3847 | xargs kill -9`
   - **sudo required for pm2 startup**: Can't run sudo from terminal — Fixed by creating LaunchAgent plist directly (no sudo needed for user agents)
   - **Playground TypeScript errors**: unused UnifiedAgent import, `fileName` → `filename`, status type string vs union — All fixed
   - **Agent routing table broken**: Global CLAUDE.md had `factory`, `researcher`, `stack-shopify` — Fixed with correct filenames: rex, nova, koda, etc.

5. Problem Solving:
   - **Orchestration producing meta-commentary**: Root cause was vague `"Provide your response:"` directive. Fixed with explicit "Produce the actual deliverable directly. Do NOT write meta-commentary" directive plus separate sections for base instructions, node task, context
   - **Agents not accessible in VS Code**: Explained the agents/commands distinction. Global CLAUDE.md now has correct agent filenames so Claude knows to route automatically
   - **Zero-setup agent calling**: Solved via SDK + pm2 + LaunchAgent — agents callable from any project without starting anything manually

6. All User Messages:
   - "Orchestration functionality and all i see still not done proper UI UX and proper flow till end and validate it. just fix all. this page should be fully functional and all"
   - "start from left"
   - "how agent orchestration work on that page put guide how it works"
   - "run task in orchestration can we optimize i mean way of working with it? also how it works?"
   - "fix it" (re: JSON parsing error)
   - [screenshot of orchestration with bad final output] "see final output give me that how to fix it"
   - "i want to test all global agent so i can also enhance quality and all time gy time where i can test or help me to integrate direct on vs code"
   - "in vs code for pinzo how this agent help?"
   - "so my concern is this global agent or global claude.md not in pinzo app than how it works?"
   - "in pinzo how i can test to ensure our app fully working and functional so lets guide be step by step testing thing"
   - [forwarded conversation about agent not being found] "see there no access of any agent" + "how i can access those agent easily here?"
   - [screenshot of Global CLAUDE.md] "this is global claude.md but i see all project pinzo rankora there not updated this yet"
   - "can you make it fully available so on those app i can easily call no technical set up want"
   - [forwarded conversation about Vex agent search] "see some i tried with pinzo app and just check to understand how it works and what to do"
   - "can you make sure in claude hub app all dynamic option available of what you set up from me so in future i can set up it easily with step and all? and also make documentation folder for all thing to ensure in future i can set up all perfectly"
   - "can you make sure there full documentation available where all explain step by step and also make sure all option available in set up to ensure its explain well clear with notes to ensure in future if lost anything we can get all thing" (said twice)

7. Pending Tasks:
   - Background documentation agent (ae42d1a0e6764ef00) is still running — writing comprehensive 8-file docs set (00-overview.md through 07-troubleshooting.md, 300-500+ lines each)
   - Build has NOT been run on the new Setup.tsx — need to verify it compiles cleanly

8. Current Work:
   The most recent work was a complete rebuild of `client/src/pages/Setup.tsx` to be fully comprehensive with 10 sections:
   1. Header with all-green system indicator
   2. System Health (4 StatusCards: pm2, LaunchAgent, Global Agents, SDK — each with notes and fix commands)
   3. Project SDK Status (table with Install buttons)
   4. Global Agent Roster (full table of all 12 agents)
   5. @boldteq/agents SDK (collapsibles: basic usage, all functions, manual install)
   6. Slash Commands (collapsibles: how they work, Pinzo's commands, adding agent wrappers)
   7. Orchestration Quick Reference
   8. pm2 & LaunchAgent Reference (collapsibles including Fresh Machine Setup)
   9. Global CLAUDE.md (required sections, edit location)
   10. Troubleshooting (7 issues) + Docs Reference table

   Simultaneously, a background agent was spawned to write 8 comprehensive documentation files (300-500+ lines each) in `claude-hub/docs/`.

9. Optional Next Step:
   The background docs agent is still running. Once it completes, need to:
   1. Run `npm run build` to verify Setup.tsx compiles cleanly
   2. Restart Claude Hub (`pm2 restart claude-hub`) so the new backend endpoints and built frontend are live
   3. Verify the Setup & Status page shows all green at `http://localhost:5173/setup`

## What Is This System?

The Boldteq Software Factory is a local AI-powered development infrastructure that runs on your Mac. It turns Claude Code (the VS Code extension) from a general-purpose assistant into a coordinated team of 12 specialist agents that know your stack, your standards, and your active projects.

Every component in this system has one job. They are designed to work together without requiring you to repeat context.

---

## The Five Components

### 1. Claude Hub — The Control Center

**Location:** `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/claude-hub/`

Claude Hub is a local web application running on `http://localhost:3847`. It has two parts:

- **Express backend** (`src/server.js`) — REST API that reads/writes agent files, CLAUDE.md files, slash commands, and handles orchestration runs and playground agent calls.
- **React/TypeScript/Vite frontend** (`client/`) — The browser dashboard you use to manage everything.

Claude Hub is kept alive 24/7 by pm2 and auto-starts on macOS login via a LaunchAgent. You never manually start it.

Pages in the dashboard:
- **Dashboard** — overview of all projects, agents, and commands
- **All Agents** — browse and edit all 12 global agents
- **All Commands** — browse slash commands across all projects
- **Orchestration** — visual DAG workflow builder for chaining agents
- **Playground** — test any single agent interactively
- **Global CLAUDE.md** — view and edit the global instruction file
- **Project Detail** — per-project agents, commands, and CLAUDE.md
- **Setup & Status** — system health, SDK installer, project directories
- **Settings** — project directory configuration

### 2. Global CLAUDE.md — The Briefing File

**Location:** `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`

Every single Claude Code session in every project reads this file first. It contains the Boldteq identity, build standards, agent routing rules, and active project list. It is the foundation that makes Claude Code behave consistently across all projects. Without it, Claude Code has no knowledge of your stack, agents, or standards.

### 3. The Agent Roster — The Specialist Team

**Location:** `~/.claude/agents/`

12 `.md` files, each one a specialist persona with a name, model, and system prompt. Claude Code loads all of them at startup and can route tasks to the right specialist automatically. You can also invoke them explicitly by name. The agents cover the entire build lifecycle from research to deployment to monitoring.

### 4. The SDK — Programmatic Agent Access

**Location:** `claude-hub/sdk/` (installed as `@boldteq/agents` in each project)

A tiny Node.js package that lets any project call any agent over HTTP with one line of code. It posts to Claude Hub which runs `claude -p` with the agent's instructions and streams back the result. Zero cost beyond the existing Claude subscription.

### 5. Slash Commands — Repeatable Workflows

**Location:** `[project]/.claude/commands/`

`.md` files that become `/commandname` shortcuts in Claude Code chat. Pinzo has `/feature`, `/fix`, `/review`, and `/db`. These are pre-written, detailed instructions for the most common workflows in that project. You type the command, pass arguments, and Claude Code executes the full workflow.

## How All Components Connect

| Component | Who reads it | Who writes it | When |
|-----------|-------------|---------------|------|
| `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` | Claude Code (every session) | You / Claude Hub | Before every task |
| `~/.claude/agents/*.md` | Claude Code (at startup) | You / Claude Hub | When invoked by name |
| `[project]/CLAUDE.md` | Claude Code (when project opens) | You / Claude Hub | When task runs in that project |
| `[project]/.claude/commands/*.md` | Claude Code (when you type `/cmd`) | You / Claude Hub | On demand |
| Claude Hub backend | Your browser, the SDK, orchestration engine | Server restarts | Always running |
| `@boldteq/agents` SDK | Your project's Node code | npm install | When `callAgent()` is called |
| pm2 | LaunchAgent, your terminal | You | On system startup |

## The Build Lifecycle

Every product build follows this loop:

```
Brief (Yash) 
  → Rex routes the work
    → Nova researches competitors
    → Arya designs the architecture
    → Riko scaffolds the project
    → Koda builds features
    → Luna writes tests
    → Sage reviews quality
    → Bolt deploys
    → Quill writes copy
    → Hawk sets up monitoring
    → Mira extracts lessons
```

All of these agents are available in Claude Code automatically. You can also run multi-step pipelines using Orchestration in Claude Hub.

## Quick Health Check

Run this to verify the entire system is working:

```bash
# 1. Is Claude Hub running?
curl -s http://localhost:3847/api/global/agents | head -c 100
# Expected: JSON array starting with [{"filename":"arya",...

# 2. Is pm2 managing it?
pm2 status
# Expected: claude-hub row with status "online"

# 3. Is LaunchAgent registered?
launchctl list | grep claude-hub
# Expected: a line with io.boldteq.claude-hub

# 4. Do global agents exist?
ls ~/.claude/agents/
# Expected: 12 .md files

# 5. Is Claude CLI available?
claude --version
# Expected: version string

2	
3	## Global Agents
4	
5	All 12 global agents live in `~/.claude/agents/`. They are automatically available in every Claude Code session across all projects.
6	
7	| Filename | Name | Model | Purpose |
8	|----------|------|-------|---------|
9	| `rex.md` | Rex — Commander | opus | Master orchestrator. Entry point for any new project or sprint. Routes to other agents in the correct order. |
10	| `nova.md` | Nova — Market Research | sonnet | Competitive intelligence. Run before building anything new. Returns competitor analysis, pricing, USP opportunities. |
11	| `arya.md` | Arya — Architecture & Planning | opus | Stack selection, data model, API design, auth/billing strategy, sprint planning. Converts research into a buildable plan. |
12	| `riko.md` | Riko — Project Setup | sonnet | Scaffolds a runnable project from Arya's plan. Sets up CI/CD, error tracking, hooks, seed data. |
13	| `koda.md` | Koda — Feature Builder | sonnet | All production code — frontend, backend, database, integrations. Reads CLAUDE.md and memory first. |
14	| `vex.md` | Vex — Bug Fixer | sonnet | Debugging specialist. Diagnoses root causes across all stacks. Has an error encyclopedia for Supabase, Stripe, Shopify, AI SDK. |
15	| `luna.md` | Luna — Testing | sonnet | Writes unit, integration, and E2E tests. Tests that catch real bugs, not coverage theater. |
16	| `sage.md` | Sage — Code Review | opus | Quality gate. Audits security, TypeScript strictness, performance, accessibility, GDPR. Blocks deploys on critical findings. |
17	| `bolt.md` | Bolt — Deployment | sonnet | Vercel, Railway, Supabase production hardening, zero-downtime migrations, Shopify submission. Requires Sage sign-off. |
18	| `quill.md` | Quill — Content & Copy | sonnet | App Store listings, landing pages, Product Hunt, SEO, onboarding, email sequences, microcopy. |
19	| `mira.md` | Mira — Memory & Training | sonnet | Knowledge extraction. Runs after every build to update `~/.claude/memory/` so all agents learn permanently. |
20	| `hawk.md` | Hawk — Monitoring & Ops | sonnet | Post-launch ops — uptime, error tracking, Core Web Vitals, AI cost monitoring, incident response. |
21	
22	## Example Usage
23	
24	Invoke any agent in Claude Code by calling it with `@agent-name` or via the SDK:
25	
26	```bash
27	# In Claude Code chat — call an agent directly
28	@koda Build the subscription billing page for Rankora
29	@nova Research AI resume screening tools — top 5 competitors
30	@sage Review the auth flow in Pinzo for security issues
31	```
32	
33	## How to Create a New Agent
34	
35	Create a `.md` file in `~/.claude/agents/` (global) or `[project]/.claude/agents/` (project-scoped).
36	
37	### Frontmatter format
38	
39	```markdown
40	---
41	name: Agent Display Name
42	description: What this agent does. Be specific — Claude Code uses this to auto-route tasks.
43	model: sonnet
44	tools: Read,Write,Edit,Bash,Glob,Grep
45	---
46	
47	Your agent's system prompt goes here.
48	
49	Write it as if briefing a senior specialist. Include:
50	- Their role and identity
51	- Their exact responsibilities
52	- What they should NOT do
53	- Standards they must follow
54	- Patterns to use (or avoid)
55	```
56	
57	### Required fields
58	
59	- `name` — display name shown in Claude Hub
60	- `description` — used by Claude Code for automatic routing; make it precise
61	- `model` — `sonnet` for speed/cost, `opus` for complex reasoning
62	
63	### Optional fields
64	
65	- `tools` — restrict which tools the agent can use (default: all)
66	
67	## Automatic Loading
68	
69	Claude Code reads all `.md` files in `~/.claude/agents/` at startup. No registration needed. Any agent you drop in that directory is immediately available in all sessions.
70	
71	## Project-Level vs Global Agents
72	
73	- **Global** (`~/.claude/agents/`) — available everywhere, all projects
74	- **Project-level** (`[project]/.claude/agents/`) — only available when working in that project
75	
76	Project agents override global agents with the same filename. Use project agents for project-specific personas or highly specialized task context.
77

2	
3	## What It Is
4	
5	A tiny Node.js package that lets any Boldteq project call any Claude agent over HTTP. Claude Hub acts as the agent runner — the SDK is just the client.
6	
7	The SDK requires Claude Hub to be running. Because Claude Hub is managed by pm2 and auto-starts on login via LaunchAgent, the SDK just works without any setup per project.
8	
9	## Installing in a New Project
10	
11	### Option A — Claude Hub UI (recommended)
12	
13	1. Open http://localhost:3847
14	2. Go to **Setup & Status**
15	3. Find your project in the table
16	4. Click **Install** — it writes the dependency and runs `npm install` for you
17	
18	### Option B — Manual
19	
20	Add to your project's `package.json`:
21	
22	```json
23	{
24	  "dependencies": {
25	    "@boldteq/agents": "file:../claude-hub/sdk"
26	  }
27	}
28	```
29	
30	The relative path must point from your project root to `claude-hub/sdk`. Then:
31	
32	```bash
33	npm install
34	```
35	
36	## API Reference
37	
38	### `callAgent(agentName, prompt, timeoutMs?)`
39	
40	Call any global agent with a task. Returns a promise.
41	
42	```typescript
43	import { callAgent } from '@boldteq/agents'
44	
45	const result = await callAgent('quill', 'Write App Store listing for Pinzo')
46	
47	if (result.success) {
48	  console.log(result.output)  // the agent's response
49	} else {
50	  console.error(result.error) // what went wrong
51	}
52	```
53	
54	**Parameters**
55	
56	| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
57	|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
58	| `agentName` | `string` | — | Agent filename without `.md` (e.g. `'koda'`, `'quill'`) |
59	| `prompt` | `string` | — | The task or instruction for the agent |
60	| `timeoutMs` | `number` | `120000` | Timeout in milliseconds (2 minutes default) |
61	
62	**Returns: `AgentResult`**
63	
64	```typescript
65	interface AgentResult {
66	  success: boolean
67	  output: string   // agent's response text
68	  agent: string    // the agent name that ran
69	  error?: string   // set if success is false
70	}
71	```
72	
73	---
74	
75	### `listAgents()`
76	
77	Fetch all available global agents from Claude Hub.
78	
79	```typescript
80	import { listAgents } from '@boldteq/agents'
81	
82	const agents = await listAgents()
83	// [{ filename: 'koda', name: 'Koda — Feature Builder', description: '...', model: 'sonnet', body: '...' }]
84	```
85	
86	Returns an empty array if Claude Hub is unreachable.
87	
88	---
89	
90	### `isOnline()`
91	
92	Check if Claude Hub is reachable. Useful as a health guard before calling agents.
93	
94	```typescript
95	import { isOnline } from '@boldteq/agents'
96	
97	if (await isOnline()) {
98	  const result = await callAgent('nova', 'Research competitors')
99	}
100	```
101	
102	Returns `true` / `false`. Uses a 3-second timeout.
103	
104	## TypeScript Usage
105	
106	The SDK ships with full TypeScript declarations in `index.d.ts`. Import types directly:
107	
108	```typescript
109	import { callAgent, listAgents, isOnline } from '@boldteq/agents'
110	import type { AgentResult, Agent } from '@boldteq/agents'
111	
112	async function generateCopy(productName: string): Promise<string> {
113	  const result: AgentResult = await callAgent(
114	    'quill',
115	    `Write a one-sentence tagline for ${productName}`
116	  )
117	  if (!result.success) throw new Error(result.error)
118	  return result.output
119	}
120	```
121	
122	## Error Handling
123	
124	The SDK never throws. It always returns an `AgentResult`. Check `result.success`:
125	
126	```typescript
127	const result = await callAgent('koda', 'Build the auth flow')
128	
129	if (!result.success) {
130	  if (result.error?.includes('not reachable')) {
131	    // Claude Hub is down
132	    console.error('Start Claude Hub: pm2 start claude-hub')
133	  } else if (result.error?.includes('Timed out')) {
134	    // Agent ran too long — increase timeout or break task into smaller steps
135	    const retry = await callAgent('koda', 'Build auth flow', 180000)
136	  } else {
137	    console.error('Agent error:', result.error)
138	  }
139	}
140	```
141	
142	## CLAUDE_HUB_URL Environment Variable
143	
144	By default the SDK connects to `http://localhost:3847`. Override this for remote or non-standard setups:
145	
146	```bash
147	# .env
148	CLAUDE_HUB_URL=http://192.168.1.10:3847
149	```
150	
151	```typescript
152	// SDK reads it automatically at require/import time
153	import { callAgent } from '@boldteq/agents'
154	// now calls http://192.168.1.10:3847
155	```
156	
157	This allows Claude Hub to run on a separate machine (e.g. a dev server) while projects consume it over the local network.

2	
3	## What Are Slash Commands?
4	
5	Slash commands are project-specific prompts stored as `.md` files in `[project]/.claude/commands/`. When you type `/command-name` in Claude Code, it runs that file's content as a prompt.
6	
7	They are different from agents:
8	
9	| | Agents | Slash Commands |
10	|-|--------|---------------|
11	| **Location** | `~/.claude/agents/` or `.claude/agents/` | `.claude/commands/` |
12	| **Scope** | Global or project | Project-only |
13	| **Invoked by** | Claude Code routing or `@agent-name` | `/command-name` |
14	| **Purpose** | Persistent specialist persona | Repeatable workflow step |
15	| **Has identity?** | Yes — name, model, description | No — just instructions |
16	
17	Use agents when you need a specialist persona that Claude Code auto-routes to. Use slash commands for project-specific workflows you run repeatedly (build a feature, fix a bug, review code, run a migration).
18	
19	## The `$ARGUMENTS` Placeholder
20	
21	Commands accept freeform input via `$ARGUMENTS`. When you run `/feature Build subscription billing`, the entire string `Build subscription billing` replaces every `$ARGUMENTS` in the file.
22	
23	```markdown
24	<!-- .claude/commands/feature.md -->
25	Build a complete feature for this app: $ARGUMENTS
26	
27	## Steps
28	1. Read CLAUDE.md for context
29	2. Plan the feature
30	3. Build it
31	```
32	
33	Run as: `/feature Add dark mode toggle to settings`
34	
35	## Pinzo's Commands
36	
37	Pinzo has four commands in `.claude/commands/`:
38	
39	### `/feature`
40	Builds a complete feature end-to-end. Takes a feature description as `$ARGUMENTS`. Orchestrates the right agents (builder for admin, widget-specialist for storefront), handles DB migrations, and validates the build. The most-used command in Pinzo.
41	
42	```
43	/feature Add product tagging to the admin dashboard
44	```
45	
46	### `/fix`
47	Diagnoses and fixes a bug. Pass the error message or description as `$ARGUMENTS`. Routes to vex (bug fixer) with full project context.
48	
49	```
50	/fix TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined reading 'shop' in webhook handler
51	```
52	
53	### `/review`
54	Reviews a piece of code or a file for quality, security, and adherence to Pinzo's standards. Routes to sage (code review).
55	
56	```
57	/review src/routes/api.products.tsx
58	```
59	
60	### `/db`
61	Database workflow command. Handles Prisma migrations, schema changes, and seeding. Takes a migration description as `$ARGUMENTS`.
62	
63	```
64	/db Add index on orders.shop for performance
65	```
66	
67	## Creating a New Command
68	
69	1. Create a `.md` file in `[project]/.claude/commands/`
70	2. Write instructions using `$ARGUMENTS` as the input placeholder
71	3. The filename (without `.md`) becomes the slash command name
72	
73	### Example: A deploy command
74	
75	```bash
76	# File: .claude/commands/deploy.md
77	```
78	
79	```markdown
80	Deploy $ARGUMENTS to production.
81	
82	## Pre-deploy checklist
83	1. Run `npm run build` and confirm zero errors
84	2. Run `npm test` — all tests must pass
85	3. Check for any hardcoded secrets or TODOs
86	4. Confirm environment variables are set in Vercel/Railway
87	5. Run the deploy command: `vercel --prod` or `railway up`
88	6. Smoke test: verify the live URL loads, auth works, billing page loads
89	
90	Report the deploy URL when done.
91	```
92	
93	Run: `/deploy Pinzo v1.2 — adds CSV export`
94	
95	### Naming conventions
96	
97	- Use lowercase with hyphens: `release-notes`, `db-migrate`, `type-check`
98	- Keep names short — you type them often
99	- One command per workflow, not one command per file
100	
101	### Scoping
102	
103	Commands only work in the project where they live. A command in `Pinzo/.claude/commands/` is not available in `Rankora/`. If you want a command everywhere, it needs to live in each project (or become a global agent).
104

2	
3	## What It Does
4	
5	Orchestration chains multiple agents together as a visual pipeline. Each node runs one agent with a specific instruction. The output of one node feeds into the next. You write a single task at the top and each agent refines or extends it.
6	
7	This is useful for multi-step content or code generation where you want distinct specialists at each stage rather than one agent doing everything.
8	
9	## How to Use It
10	
11	1. Open **Orchestration** in the sidebar
12	2. Click **New** to create a pipeline (or load an existing one)
13	3. Add nodes — each node is one agent step
14	4. Connect nodes with arrows to define flow
15	5. Enter your top-level task in the **Task** input
16	6. Click **Run** — watch each node execute in sequence
17	7. Click any completed node to see its full output
18	
19	## The Research → Write → Polish Template
20	
21	The built-in template chains three agents:
22	
23	```
24	[Task Input] → Nova (research) → Quill (draft) → Quill (polish)
25	```
26	
27	1. **Nova** researches the topic and extracts key facts, positioning, and angles
28	2. **Quill** drafts content using Nova's research output as context
29	3. **Quill** polishes the draft for tone, clarity, and persuasion
30	
31	Use this for: App Store listings, landing page copy, Product Hunt posts, blog posts.
32	
33	## Key Tips
34	
35	- **Start nodes are free** — the first node (task input) passes your text through without running an agent. Use it as context for downstream nodes.

3	## What is Agent Orchestration?
4	
5	Agent Orchestration is a **visual workflow system** that chains multiple Claude agents (or custom tasks) together in a directed graph. Each node processes the output of its upstream nodes and passes its result downstream.
6	
7	Think of it as: **Task → Agent 1 → Agent 2 → Agent 3 → Final Output**
8	
9	---
10	
11	## How It Works (Step-by-Step)
12	
13	### 1. **You Build the Graph**
14	
15	You add nodes to a canvas and connect them with edges:
16	
17	```
18	┌──────────────┐
19	│  Task Input  │  (Your initial prompt)
20	└──────────────┘
21	       │
22	       ↓
23	┌──────────────┐
24	│  Planner     │  (Breaks task into steps)
25	└──────────────┘
26	       │
27	       ↓
28	┌──────────────┐
29	│  Developer   │  (Writes code based on plan)
30	└──────────────┘
31	       │
32	       ↓
33	┌──────────────┐
34	│  Reviewer    │  (Audits and improves code)
35	└──────────────┘
36	       │
37	       ↓
38	   FINAL OUTPUT
39	```
40	
41	### 2. **Execution Flow (Backend)**

46	```javascript
47	// 1. Receive nodes and edges from frontend

57	// 3. Topologically sort nodes (determine execution order)
58	// Makes sure:
59	// - Start nodes run first
60	// - Dependencies are respected
61	// - No cycles (DAG - Directed Acyclic Graph)
62	order = [node-1, node-2, node-3, ...]

89	  
90	  // Build context from upstream outputs
91	  if node has incoming edges:
92	    context = merge all upstream node outputs
93	  else:
94	    context = initial task

96	  // Construct the full prompt
97	  fullPrompt = instructions + "\n\n---\n\n" + context + "\nProvide your response:"
98

100	  send { type: 'start', nodeId, label }

103	  output = await runClaudeSync(fullPrompt)
104	  
105	  // Store result for downstream nodes
106	  results[nodeId] = output
107	  
108	  // Send "done" event with output
109	  send { type: 'done', nodeId, label, output }

313	## Optimization Guide: Best Practices
314	
315	### 1. **Minimize Redundant Work**
316	❌ **Bad**: Task → Researcher → Developer → Researcher → Developer
317	✅ **Good**: Task → Researcher → Developer
318	
319	Fan-out once to parallelize (conceptually), but don't re-process.
320	
321	### 2. **Keep Node Instructions Focused**
322	❌ **Bad Instructions**:
323	```
324	"Do research, write code, review it, optimize, test everything"
325	```
326	
327	✅ **Good Instructions**:
328	```
329	"You are a research expert. Identify the best libraries, patterns, 
330	and approaches for this task. Output concise recommendations."
331	```
332	
333	Each node = one clear responsibility.
334	
335	### 3. **Use Agent Nodes Over Custom Steps (When Possible)**
336	❌ **Slower**:
337	```
338	Custom node with instructions: "Plan the task..."
339	Custom node with instructions: "Write code..."
340	Custom node with instructions: "Review code..."
341	```
342	
343	✅ **Faster** (agents are pre-optimized):
344	```
345	Custom planning node
346	→ Koda (Builder agent - optimized for coding)
347	→ Sage (Review agent - optimized for validation)
348	```
349	
350	Agents have battle-tested instructions. Custom steps need YOU to write good prompts.
351	
352	### 4. **Structure Graphs for Parallelism (Conceptually)**
353	```
354	Task 
355	  → Branch A (Planner)
356	  → Branch B (Researcher)
357	  
358	Both A and B run conceptually in parallel (though sequentially in implementation).
359	Join at Node C (Developer) which receives both outputs.
360	```
361	
362	This gives Claude **more diverse context** than serial execution.
363	
364	### 5. **Limit Context Size**
365	⚠️ **Problem**: If Node 1 outputs 10KB, Node 2 outputs 15KB, Node 3 receives 25KB of context.
366	- Large contexts slow down Claude
367	- Token usage increases
368	- Can hit context limits
369	
370	✅ **Solution**: Add a "Summarizer" step:
371	```
372	Node 1: Researcher → outputs 10KB research
373	Node 2: Summarizer → "Summarize the above into key points" → outputs 500B
374	Node 3: Developer → receives only key summary, not all research
375	```
376	
377	### 6. **Add Validation Nodes**
378	```
379	Task → Developer → Validator → Done
380	
381	Validator checks:
382	- Does output parse as valid JSON?
383	- Does code have syntax errors?
384	- Does response answer the original question?
385	
386	If validation fails, you know exactly where to re-run.
387	```
388	
389	### 7. **Use Custom Steps for Complex Logic**
390	```
391	Custom Step: "Parse the code output and extract only the function definition"
392	→ Reduces noise for next node
393	→ Cheaper than having next agent parse it
394	```
395	
396	### 8. **Avoid Circular Dependencies**
397	⚠️ **Invalid** (Orchestration will reject):
398	```
399	A → B → C → A  (creates a cycle)
400	```
401	
402	✅ **Valid** (DAG only):
403	```
404	A → B → C (linear)
405	A → B
406	A → C  (fan-out)
407	B → D
408	C → D  (fan-in)
409	```
410	
411	### 9. **Set Appropriate Task Inputs**
412	❌ **Too vague**:
413	```
414	"Build an app"
415	```
416	
417	✅ **Specific & Detailed**:
418	```
419	"Build a React hook for pagination with TypeScript.
420	Requirements:
421	- Support custom items per page
422	- Return { currentPage, setCurrentPage, pageItems, totalPages }
423	- Handle edge cases (empty items, invalid page)
424	- Include TypeScript generics"
425	```
426	
427	Better inputs → better outputs from all nodes.
428	
429	### 10. **Use Save/Load for Templates**
430	```
431	1. Build optimized orchestration (Plan → Code → Review)
432	2. Save it
433	3. Reuse with different tasks:
434	   - "Build a React hook..."
435	   - "Build an API endpoint..."
436	   - "Build a CLI tool..."
437	
438	Same structure, different inputs = faster iteration.
439	```

467	
468	### Pattern 1: Multi-Output Synthesis
469	```
470	Task
471	  → Researcher A: "Find solutions in Language A"
472	  → Researcher B: "Find solutions in Language B"

478	**Benefit**: Explores solution space more thoroughly than single researcher.

481	```
482	Task
483	  → First Pass (Developer)
484	  → Quality Check (Reviewer)
485	  → If issues found → go back to Developer with feedback
486	  → (Manual re-run with revised inputs)
487	```
488	
489	**Limitation**: Current system is one-pass (no loops). To iterate, you manually re-run with feedback.
490	
491	### Pattern 3: Error Recovery
492	```
493	Task
494	  → Developer
495	  → Validator (checks if output is valid)
496	  → If invalid: trigger manual re-run with debugging prompt
497	```
498	
499	### Pattern 4: Cascading Specialization
500	```
501	Task (general)
502	  → Planner (breaks into sub-tasks)
503	  → Specialist A (handles part 1)
504	  → Specialist B (handles part 2)
505	  → Specialist C (handles part 3)
506	  → Integrator (combines results)
507	```
508	
509	**Benefit**: Each specialist is more focused, produces better output.

513	## Common Mistakes & Fixes
514	
515	| Mistake | Problem | Fix |
516	|---------|---------|-----|
517	| Circular edges | System rejects, can't run | Use DAG only (no cycles) |
518	| No edges (disconnected nodes) | Nodes ignore each other | Connect nodes with edges |
519	| Too many nodes in series | Each node takes 20s+ → slow | Use fan-out/fan-in patterns |
520	| Generic instructions | Agent doesn't understand intent | Write specific, detailed prompts |
521	| Overloading one node | "Do X, Y, Z, A, B, C" | Split into separate nodes |
522	| Storing huge outputs | Context balloons | Use summarizer nodes between steps |
523	| Re-querying same source | Wasted API calls | Cache in first node, reuse output |

530	```
531	"Do something useful with this information"
532	```

540	3. Type mismatches in function calls
541	4. Union type handling

546	### ✅ **Better**
547	```
548	"You are a TypeScript code reviewer specializing in type safety. 
549	Your job is to ensure all code is fully typed.
550	
551	Rules:
552	- No implicit 'any' allowed
553	- All function parameters must be typed
554	- Return types must be explicit
555	- Generic constraints should be clear
556	
557	Analyze the provided code and output:
558	1. List of type safety issues (if any)
559	2. Severity (critical / warning)
560	3. Suggested fixes
561	
562	If the code is perfect, respond: 'Type safety: ✅ PASS'"
563	```
564	
565	**Key**: Be specific about what you want, how to structure the output, and what "done" looks like.

569	## FAQ
570	
571	### Q: Can I run nodes in parallel?
572	**A**: Conceptually, nodes with independent upstream sources (fan-out) run in parallel *conceptually*. 
573	However, the backend executes them sequentially for simplicity. Each node still gets context from all its upstream sources.
574	
575	If you need true parallelism, that's a future enhancement.
576	
577	### Q: What if a node times out?
578	**A**: Nodes have a **120-second timeout**. If a Claude execution takes longer, the node fails with:
579	```
580	"Node execution timed out after 120s"
581	```
582	
583	Fix: Simplify the task, give more specific instructions, or break into smaller nodes.
584	
585	### Q: Can I edit a node's instruction during a run?
586	**A**: No. Orchestration is **immutable during execution**. 
587	To change instructions, stop the run, edit the node, and re-run.
588	
589	### Q: How do I debug a failed node?
590	**A**: 
591	1. Click the failed node (it turns red)
592	2. Scroll the run log to see the error message
593	3. Edit the node's instructions to be clearer
594	4. Click **Reset** in the run panel
595	5. Click **Re-run** to execute again with new instructions
596	
597	### Q: Can I save intermediate results?
598	**A**: Yes! The run log shows every node's output. Click **View full output** to see and copy any node's result.
599	
600	### Q: Can I use orchestration for real-time tasks?
601	**A**: No. Each node waits for the previous to complete. If you need streaming responses within a task, that's a different feature (not yet implemented).
602	
603	### Q: What's the cost of running a 5-node pipeline?
604	**A**: ~$0.02-0.05 per run (depends on task complexity and output length). Each node makes one Claude API call.

## Your Role
You own outcomes, not tasks. Yash gives you a brief — one line or ten — and you turn it into coordinated execution across the full agent team. You never write code, research markets, or design architecture. You sequence, delegate, and enforce quality gates.

## Operating Modes

### Mode A: New Product Build
Triggered when: new app, new SaaS, new Shopify app
Loop: Nova → Arya → Riko → Koda → Luna → Sage → Bolt → Mira

### Mode B: Feature Addition
Triggered when: existing project needs a new feature
Loop: Arya (scoping only) → Koda → Luna → Sage → Bolt → Mira

### Mode C: Maintenance / Fix Sprint
Triggered when: bugs, performance issues, security patches, dependency updates
Loop: Vex (diagnosis) → Koda (fix) → Luna (regression test) → Sage (verify) → Bolt (deploy)

### Mode D: Launch / Go-Live
Triggered when: product is built and needs to ship
Loop: Sage (final audit) → Quill (app store / landing copy) → Bolt (deploy) → Hawk (monitoring setup)

Identify the mode first. State it. Then execute.

## Step 1: Load Memory (Every Mode)
Before dispatching any agent:
- Read `~/.claude/memory/MEMORY.md` for relevant patterns
- Load the matching stack file from `~/.claude/memory/stacks/`
- Check `~/.claude/memory/patterns/avoid/antipatterns.md`
- Apply all accumulated knowledge — solved problems stay solved

## Step 2: Classify the Project (Mode A only)
- Shopify App → Stack B: Remix + Prisma + Polaris + Shopify Billing
- SaaS Web App → Stack A: Next.js 14+ + Supabase + Stripe + Vercel
- AI-Heavy App → Stack C: Next.js + Supabase + Vercel AI SDK + Anthropic/OpenAI + Edge Functions
- Hybrid or novel → Propose a stack with justification. Confirm with Yash before proceeding.

## Step 3: Research (Mode A only — dispatch Nova)
Brief Nova with: product category, target market, any known competitors.
Expect back: competitor analysis, pricing patterns, table stakes features, USP gap, V1 recommendations.
Do not proceed to architecture without Nova's output.

## Step 4: Architecture (Mode A + B — dispatch Arya)
Pass to Arya: Nova's research (if Mode A), project constraints, stack.
Expect back: data model, API routes, auth strategy, billing strategy, V1 scope, sprint plan.
For Mode C/D, Arya scopes the change only — no full redesign.

## Step 5: Present Plan (Mode A only — wait for Yash approval)
```
PRODUCT: [name]

```
Wait for approval before building. Do not skip this gate.

## Step 6: Execute Build

### Parallel-Safe Execution
Some work can run in parallel — flag it explicitly:
- Riko (scaffold) → unblocked immediately after approval
- Quill (landing copy) → can run parallel to Koda after Arya's output
- Luna (test setup) → can run parallel to Koda's later features

### Sequential Dependencies
- Types before DB, DB before API, API before UI (Koda's internal order)
- Sage must complete before Bolt
- Bolt must complete before Hawk

### Dispatch Order (Mode A)
1. **Riko** — scaffold: folder structure, configs, auth boilerplate, billing boilerplate, CI/CD, Sentry, seed data
2. **Koda** — features in build order from Arya's sprint plan (types → DB → API → UI per feature)
3. **Quill** — copy for onboarding, empty states, CTAs, in-app microcopy (can run in parallel to Koda's later sprints)
4. **Luna** — tests for auth, billing, core feature, data validation
5. **Sage** — pre-deploy audit: security, TypeScript, error handling, a11y, GDPR
6. **Bolt** — deploy with monitoring setup

## Step 7: Train (Every Mode)

### For Schema Changes
1. Read `prisma/schema.prisma` first — understand current state

3. Edit `prisma/schema.prisma`

5. Run `npx prisma generate` (to update TypeScript types)
6. Update any route files that reference changed models
7. Run `npm run typecheck` — fix any type errors from schema changes

### For Query Optimization
1. Check existing queries in route files
2. Add indexes for frequently queried fields
3. Use `select` to fetch only needed fields (not full records)
4. Use `include` sparingly — avoid N+1 queries
5. Use `db.$transaction()` for multi-step operations

### For Data Operations
1. Always include `where: { shop: session.shop }` for security
2. Use `upsert` for singleton records (WidgetConfig, Subscription)
3. Use `createMany` for bulk inserts (ZIP code imports)
4. Use `deleteMany` for bulk deletes with proper `where` clause
5. Use transactions for multi-step operations: `db.$transaction([...])`

### Query Patterns
```tsx
// Singleton upsert (WidgetConfig, Subscription)
await db.widgetConfig.upsert({
  where: { shop: session.shop },
  update: { ...configData },
  create: { shop: session.shop, ...configData },
});

// Paginated list
const [items, total] = await db.$transaction([
  db.zipCode.findMany({
    where: { shop: session.shop },
    skip: (page - 1) * pageSize,
    take: pageSize,
    orderBy: { createdAt: "desc" },
  }),
  db.zipCode.count({ where: { shop: session.shop } }),
]);

// Bulk import with conflict handling
await db.zipCode.createMany({
  data: zipCodes.map(zc => ({ shop: session.shop, ...zc })),
  skipDuplicates: true,
});

// Safe delete (verify ownership)
await db.zipCode.deleteMany({
  where: { id: { in: ids }, shop: session.shop },
});
```

### SQLite vs PostgreSQL Gotchas
- SQLite: no `ENUM` type — use string fields with application-level validation
- SQLite: no `@db.Text` — just use `String`

- Both: `DateTime` defaults work, but format differs — Prisma handles this
- Migrations: test on SQLite in dev, but be aware PostgreSQL may need different migration

- NEVER run `npx prisma migrate reset` without explicit user confirmation — it deletes ALL data
- NEVER modify `Session` model — it's managed by `@shopify/shopify-app-session-storage-prisma`
- Always check existing migrations before creating new ones
- Always back up dev.db before destructive operations

## What Is This System?

The Boldteq Software Factory is a local AI-powered development infrastructure that runs on your Mac. It turns Claude Code (the VS Code extension) from a general-purpose assistant into a coordinated team of 12 specialist agents that know your stack, your standards, and your active projects.

Every component in this system has one job. They are designed to work together without requiring you to repeat context.

---

## The Five Components

### 1. Claude Hub — The Control Center

**Location:** `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/claude-hub/`

Claude Hub is a local web application running on `http://localhost:3847`. It has two parts:

- **Express backend** (`src/server.js`) — REST API that reads/writes agent files, CLAUDE.md files, slash commands, and handles orchestration runs and playground agent calls.
- **React/TypeScript/Vite frontend** (`client/`) — The browser dashboard you use to manage everything.

Claude Hub is kept alive 24/7 by pm2 and auto-starts on macOS login via a LaunchAgent. You never manually start it.

Pages in the dashboard:
- **Dashboard** — overview of all projects, agents, and commands
- **All Agents** — browse and edit all 12 global agents
- **All Commands** — browse slash commands across all projects
- **Orchestration** — visual DAG workflow builder for chaining agents
- **Playground** — test any single agent interactively
- **Global CLAUDE.md** — view and edit the global instruction file
- **Project Detail** — per-project agents, commands, and CLAUDE.md
- **Setup & Status** — system health, SDK installer, project directories
- **Settings** — project directory configuration

### 2. Global CLAUDE.md — The Briefing File

**Location:** `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`

Every single Claude Code session in every project reads this file first. It contains the Boldteq identity, build standards, agent routing rules, and active project list. It is the foundation that makes Claude Code behave consistently across all projects. Without it, Claude Code has no knowledge of your stack, agents, or standards.

### 3. The Agent Roster — The Specialist Team

**Location:** `~/.claude/agents/`

12 `.md` files, each one a specialist persona with a name, model, and system prompt. Claude Code loads all of them at startup and can route tasks to the right specialist automatically. You can also invoke them explicitly by name. The agents cover the entire build lifecycle from research to deployment to monitoring.

### 4. The SDK — Programmatic Agent Access

**Location:** `claude-hub/sdk/` (installed as `@boldteq/agents` in each project)

A tiny Node.js package that lets any project call any agent over HTTP with one line of code. It posts to Claude Hub which runs `claude -p` with the agent's instructions and streams back the result. Zero cost beyond the existing Claude subscription.

### 5. Slash Commands — Repeatable Workflows

**Location:** `[project]/.claude/commands/`

`.md` files that become `/commandname` shortcuts in Claude Code chat. Pinzo has `/feature`, `/fix`, `/review`, and `/db`. These are pre-written, detailed instructions for the most common workflows in that project. You type the command, pass arguments, and Claude Code executes the full workflow.

| `[project]/.claude/commands/*.md` | Claude Code (when you type `/cmd`) | You / Claude Hub | On demand |
| Claude Hub backend | Your browser, the SDK, orchestration engine | Server restarts | Always running |
| `@boldteq/agents` SDK | Your project's Node code | npm install | When `callAgent()` is called |
| pm2 | LaunchAgent, your terminal | You | On system startup |

Every product build follows this loop:

```
Brief (Yash) 
  → Rex routes the work
    → Nova researches competitors
    → Arya designs the architecture
    → Riko scaffolds the project
    → Koda builds features
    → Luna writes tests
    → Sage reviews quality
    → Bolt deploys
    → Quill writes copy
    → Hawk sets up monitoring
    → Mira extracts lessons
```

All of these agents are available in Claude Code automatically. You can also run multi-step pipelines using Orchestration in Claude Hub.

## Context About the System

**Claude Hub** is a local management dashboard at `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/claude-hub/`
- Express backend (`src/server.js`) running on port 3847
- React/TypeScript/Vite frontend (`client/`)
- Manages Claude Code agents, CLAUDE.md files, slash commands across all projects
- Also has Orchestration (visual DAG workflow builder) and Playground (agent tester)
- Run via pm2 as a background service: `pm2 start ecosystem.config.js`
- Auto-starts on macOS login via LaunchAgent at `~/Library/LaunchAgents/io.boldteq.claude-hub.plist`

**The Agent System:**
- 12 global agents in `~/.claude/agents/`: rex, nova, arya, riko, koda, vex, luna, sage, bolt, quill, hawk, mira
- Each agent is a `.md` file with frontmatter: name, description, model
- Claude Code automatically loads these as sub-agents in every session
- Agents are also callable programmatically via `@boldteq/agents` SDK

**The SDK (`@boldteq/agents`):**
- Located at `claude-hub/sdk/` (package.json, index.js, index.d.ts)
- Installed in all 6 projects via `"@boldteq/agents": "file:../claude-hub/sdk"` in each project's package.json
- Usage: `const { callAgent } = require('@boldteq/agents'); await callAgent('quill', 'task')`
- Calls `POST http://localhost:3847/api/playground/run` which runs `claude -p` with agent instructions
- Zero cost — uses existing Claude subscription

**The Projects (all in `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/`):**
- Pinzo — Shopify ZIP code delivery checker (React Router 7, Polaris, Prisma)
- Rankora — AI resume ranker SaaS (React + Vite + Supabase + Dodo Payments)
- QuizSnap — Shopify product quiz app (Stack B)
- Size Chart & Recommender — Shopify size charts (Stack B)
- CROBOT — TBD
- Store Locator — TBD

**Global CLAUDE.md** at `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`:
- Loaded by Claude Code in EVERY session regardless of project
- Contains: Boldteq identity, build standards, agent roster table, routing rules, active projects
- Project CLAUDE.md files are also loaded when Claude Code opens that project

**Slash Commands:**
- Located at `.claude/commands/` inside each project
- User types `/commandname` in VS Code Claude Code chat
- `$ARGUMENTS` placeholder gets replaced with text after the command
- Pinzo has: /feature, /fix, /review, /db

2	
3	## Global Agents
4	
5	All 12 global agents live in `~/.claude/agents/`. They are automatically available in every Claude Code session across all projects.
6	
7	| Filename | Name | Model | Purpose |
8	|----------|------|-------|---------|
9	| `rex.md` | Rex — Commander | opus | Master orchestrator. Entry point for any new project or sprint. Routes to other agents in the correct order. |
10	| `nova.md` | Nova — Market Research | sonnet | Competitive intelligence. Run before building anything new. Returns competitor analysis, pricing, USP opportunities. |
11	| `arya.md` | Arya — Architecture & Planning | opus | Stack selection, data model, API design, auth/billing strategy, sprint planning. Converts research into a buildable plan. |
12	| `riko.md` | Riko — Project Setup | sonnet | Scaffolds a runnable project from Arya's plan. Sets up CI/CD, error tracking, hooks, seed data. |
13	| `koda.md` | Koda — Feature Builder | sonnet | All production code — frontend, backend, database, integrations. Reads CLAUDE.md and memory first. |
14	| `vex.md` | Vex — Bug Fixer | sonnet | Debugging specialist. Diagnoses root causes across all stacks. Has an error encyclopedia for Supabase, Stripe, Shopify, AI SDK. |
15	| `luna.md` | Luna — Testing | sonnet | Writes unit, integration, and E2E tests. Tests that catch real bugs, not coverage theater. |
16	| `sage.md` | Sage — Code Review | opus | Quality gate. Audits security, TypeScript strictness, performance, accessibility, GDPR. Blocks deploys on critical findings. |
17	| `bolt.md` | Bolt — Deployment | sonnet | Vercel, Railway, Supabase production hardening, zero-downtime migrations, Shopify submission. Requires Sage sign-off. |
18	| `quill.md` | Quill — Content & Copy | sonnet | App Store listings, landing pages, Product Hunt, SEO, onboarding, email sequences, microcopy. |
19	| `mira.md` | Mira — Memory & Training | sonnet | Knowledge extraction. Runs after every build to update `~/.claude/memory/` so all agents learn permanently. |
20	| `hawk.md` | Hawk — Monitoring & Ops | sonnet | Post-launch ops — uptime, error tracking, Core Web Vitals, AI cost monitoring, incident response. |
21	
22	## Example Usage
23	
24	Invoke any agent in Claude Code by calling it with `@agent-name` or via the SDK:
25	
26	```bash
27	# In Claude Code chat — call an agent directly
28	@koda Build the subscription billing page for Rankora
29	@nova Research AI resume screening tools — top 5 competitors
30	@sage Review the auth flow in Pinzo for security issues
31	```
32	
33	## How to Create a New Agent
34	
35	Create a `.md` file in `~/.claude/agents/` (global) or `[project]/.claude/agents/` (project-scoped).
36	
37	### Frontmatter format
38	
39	```markdown
40	---
41	name: Agent Display Name
42	description: What this agent does. Be specific — Claude Code uses this to auto-route tasks.
43	model: sonnet
44	tools: Read,Write,Edit,Bash,Glob,Grep
45	---
46	
47	Your agent's system prompt goes here.
48	
49	Write it as if briefing a senior specialist. Include:
50	- Their role and identity
51	- Their exact responsibilities
52	- What they should NOT do
53	- Standards they must follow
54	- Patterns to use (or avoid)
55	```
56	
57	### Required fields
58	
59	- `name` — display name shown in Claude Hub
60	- `description` — used by Claude Code for automatic routing; make it precise
61	- `model` — `sonnet` for speed/cost, `opus` for complex reasoning
62	
63	### Optional fields
64	
65	- `tools` — restrict which tools the agent can use (default: all)
66	
67	## Automatic Loading
68	
69	Claude Code reads all `.md` files in `~/.claude/agents/` at startup. No registration needed. Any agent you drop in that directory is immediately available in all sessions.
70	
71	## Project-Level vs Global Agents
72	
73	- **Global** (`~/.claude/agents/`) — available everywhere, all projects
74	- **Project-level** (`[project]/.claude/agents/`) — only available when working in that project
75	
76	Project agents override global agents with the same filename. Use project agents for project-specific personas or highly specialized task context.
77

2	
3	## What It Is
4	
5	A tiny Node.js package that lets any Boldteq project call any Claude agent over HTTP. Claude Hub acts as the agent runner — the SDK is just the client.
6	
7	The SDK requires Claude Hub to be running. Because Claude Hub is managed by pm2 and auto-starts on login via LaunchAgent, the SDK just works without any setup per project.
8	
9	## Installing in a New Project
10	
11	### Option A — Claude Hub UI (recommended)
12	
13	1. Open http://localhost:3847
14	2. Go to **Setup & Status**
15	3. Find your project in the table
16	4. Click **Install** — it writes the dependency and runs `npm install` for you
17	
18	### Option B — Manual
19	
20	Add to your project's `package.json`:
21	
22	```json
23	{
24	  "dependencies": {
25	    "@boldteq/agents": "file:../claude-hub/sdk"
26	  }
27	}
28	```
29	
30	The relative path must point from your project root to `claude-hub/sdk`. Then:
31	
32	```bash
33	npm install
34	```
35	
36	## API Reference
37	
38	### `callAgent(agentName, prompt, timeoutMs?)`
39	
40	Call any global agent with a task. Returns a promise.
41	
42	```typescript
43	import { callAgent } from '@boldteq/agents'
44	
45	const result = await callAgent('quill', 'Write App Store listing for Pinzo')
46	
47	if (result.success) {
48	  console.log(result.output)  // the agent's response
49	} else {
50	  console.error(result.error) // what went wrong
51	}
52	```
53	
54	**Parameters**
55	
56	| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
57	|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
58	| `agentName` | `string` | — | Agent filename without `.md` (e.g. `'koda'`, `'quill'`) |
59	| `prompt` | `string` | — | The task or instruction for the agent |
60	| `timeoutMs` | `number` | `120000` | Timeout in milliseconds (2 minutes default) |
61	
62	**Returns: `AgentResult`**
63	
64	```typescript
65	interface AgentResult {
66	  success: boolean
67	  output: string   // agent's response text
68	  agent: string    // the agent name that ran
69	  error?: string   // set if success is false
70	}
71	```
72	
73	---
74	
75	### `listAgents()`
76	
77	Fetch all available global agents from Claude Hub.
78	
79	```typescript
80	import { listAgents } from '@boldteq/agents'
81	
82	const agents = await listAgents()
83	// [{ filename: 'koda', name: 'Koda — Feature Builder', description: '...', model: 'sonnet', body: '...' }]
84	```
85	
86	Returns an empty array if Claude Hub is unreachable.
87	
88	---
89	
90	### `isOnline()`
91	
92	Check if Claude Hub is reachable. Useful as a health guard before calling agents.
93	
94	```typescript
95	import { isOnline } from '@boldteq/agents'
96	
97	if (await isOnline()) {
98	  const result = await callAgent('nova', 'Research competitors')
99	}
100	```
101	
102	Returns `true` / `false`. Uses a 3-second timeout.
103	
104	## TypeScript Usage
105	
106	The SDK ships with full TypeScript declarations in `index.d.ts`. Import types directly:
107	
108	```typescript
109	import { callAgent, listAgents, isOnline } from '@boldteq/agents'
110	import type { AgentResult, Agent } from '@boldteq/agents'
111	
112	async function generateCopy(productName: string): Promise<string> {
113	  const result: AgentResult = await callAgent(
114	    'quill',
115	    `Write a one-sentence tagline for ${productName}`
116	  )
117	  if (!result.success) throw new Error(result.error)
118	  return result.output
119	}
120	```
121	
122	## Error Handling
123	
124	The SDK never throws. It always returns an `AgentResult`. Check `result.success`:
125	
126	```typescript
127	const result = await callAgent('koda', 'Build the auth flow')
128	
129	if (!result.success) {
130	  if (result.error?.includes('not reachable')) {
131	    // Claude Hub is down
132	    console.error('Start Claude Hub: pm2 start claude-hub')
133	  } else if (result.error?.includes('Timed out')) {
134	    // Agent ran too long — increase timeout or break task into smaller steps
135	    const retry = await callAgent('koda', 'Build auth flow', 180000)
136	  } else {
137	    console.error('Agent error:', result.error)
138	  }
139	}
140	```
141	
142	## CLAUDE_HUB_URL Environment Variable
143	
144	By default the SDK connects to `http://localhost:3847`. Override this for remote or non-standard setups:
145	
146	```bash
147	# .env
148	CLAUDE_HUB_URL=http://192.168.1.10:3847
149	```
150	
151	```typescript
152	// SDK reads it automatically at require/import time
153	import { callAgent } from '@boldteq/agents'
154	// now calls http://192.168.1.10:3847
155	```
156	
157	This allows Claude Hub to run on a separate machine (e.g. a dev server) while projects consume it over the local network.

2	
3	## What Are Slash Commands?
4	
5	Slash commands are project-specific prompts stored as `.md` files in `[project]/.claude/commands/`. When you type `/command-name` in Claude Code, it runs that file's content as a prompt.
6	
7	They are different from agents:
8	
9	| | Agents | Slash Commands |
10	|-|--------|---------------|
11	| **Location** | `~/.claude/agents/` or `.claude/agents/` | `.claude/commands/` |
12	| **Scope** | Global or project | Project-only |
13	| **Invoked by** | Claude Code routing or `@agent-name` | `/command-name` |
14	| **Purpose** | Persistent specialist persona | Repeatable workflow step |
15	| **Has identity?** | Yes — name, model, description | No — just instructions |
16	
17	Use agents when you need a specialist persona that Claude Code auto-routes to. Use slash commands for project-specific workflows you run repeatedly (build a feature, fix a bug, review code, run a migration).
18	
19	## The `$ARGUMENTS` Placeholder
20	
21	Commands accept freeform input via `$ARGUMENTS`. When you run `/feature Build subscription billing`, the entire string `Build subscription billing` replaces every `$ARGUMENTS` in the file.
22	
23	```markdown
24	<!-- .claude/commands/feature.md -->
25	Build a complete feature for this app: $ARGUMENTS
26	
27	## Steps
28	1. Read CLAUDE.md for context
29	2. Plan the feature
30	3. Build it
31	```
32	
33	Run as: `/feature Add dark mode toggle to settings`
34	
35	## Pinzo's Commands
36	
37	Pinzo has four commands in `.claude/commands/`:
38	
39	### `/feature`
40	Builds a complete feature end-to-end. Takes a feature description as `$ARGUMENTS`. Orchestrates the right agents (builder for admin, widget-specialist for storefront), handles DB migrations, and validates the build. The most-used command in Pinzo.
41	
42	```
43	/feature Add product tagging to the admin dashboard
44	```
45	
46	### `/fix`
47	Diagnoses and fixes a bug. Pass the error message or description as `$ARGUMENTS`. Routes to vex (bug fixer) with full project context.
48	
49	```
50	/fix TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined reading 'shop' in webhook handler
51	```
52	
53	### `/review`
54	Reviews a piece of code or a file for quality, security, and adherence to Pinzo's standards. Routes to sage (code review).
55	
56	```
57	/review src/routes/api.products.tsx
58	```
59	
60	### `/db`
61	Database workflow command. Handles Prisma migrations, schema changes, and seeding. Takes a migration description as `$ARGUMENTS`.
62	
63	```
64	/db Add index on orders.shop for performance
65	```
66	
67	## Creating a New Command
68	
69	1. Create a `.md` file in `[project]/.claude/commands/`
70	2. Write instructions using `$ARGUMENTS` as the input placeholder
71	3. The filename (without `.md`) becomes the slash command name
72	
73	### Example: A deploy command
74	
75	```bash
76	# File: .claude/commands/deploy.md
77	```
78	
79	```markdown
80	Deploy $ARGUMENTS to production.
81	
82	## Pre-deploy checklist
83	1. Run `npm run build` and confirm zero errors
84	2. Run `npm test` — all tests must pass
85	3. Check for any hardcoded secrets or TODOs
86	4. Confirm environment variables are set in Vercel/Railway
87	5. Run the deploy command: `vercel --prod` or `railway up`
88	6. Smoke test: verify the live URL loads, auth works, billing page loads
89	
90	Report the deploy URL when done.
91	```
92	
93	Run: `/deploy Pinzo v1.2 — adds CSV export`
94	
95	### Naming conventions
96	
97	- Use lowercase with hyphens: `release-notes`, `db-migrate`, `type-check`
98	- Keep names short — you type them often
99	- One command per workflow, not one command per file
100	
101	### Scoping
102	
103	Commands only work in the project where they live. A command in `Pinzo/.claude/commands/` is not available in `Rankora/`. If you want a command everywhere, it needs to live in each project (or become a global agent).
104

2	
3	## What It Does
4	
5	Orchestration chains multiple agents together as a visual pipeline. Each node runs one agent with a specific instruction. The output of one node feeds into the next. You write a single task at the top and each agent refines or extends it.
6	
7	This is useful for multi-step content or code generation where you want distinct specialists at each stage rather than one agent doing everything.
8	
9	## How to Use It
10	
11	1. Open **Orchestration** in the sidebar
12	2. Click **New** to create a pipeline (or load an existing one)
13	3. Add nodes — each node is one agent step
14	4. Connect nodes with arrows to define flow
15	5. Enter your top-level task in the **Task** input
16	6. Click **Run** — watch each node execute in sequence
17	7. Click any completed node to see its full output
18	
19	## The Research → Write → Polish Template
20	
21	The built-in template chains three agents:
22	
23	```
24	[Task Input] → Nova (research) → Quill (draft) → Quill (polish)
25	```
26	
27	1. **Nova** researches the topic and extracts key facts, positioning, and angles
28	2. **Quill** drafts content using Nova's research output as context
29	3. **Quill** polishes the draft for tone, clarity, and persuasion
30	
31	Use this for: App Store listings, landing page copy, Product Hunt posts, blog posts.
32	
33	## Key Tips
34

3	## What is Agent Orchestration?
4	
5	Agent Orchestration is a **visual workflow system** that chains multiple Claude agents (or custom tasks) together in a directed graph. Each node processes the output of its upstream nodes and passes its result downstream.
6	
7	Think of it as: **Task → Agent 1 → Agent 2 → Agent 3 → Final Output**
8

87	  // Get agent instructions (from agent file or custom override)
88	  instructions = agentContentMap[agentName] || node.instructions
89	  
90	  // Build context from upstream outputs
91	  if node has incoming edges:
92	    context = merge all upstream node outputs
93	  else:
94	    context = initial task
95	  
96	  // Construct the full prompt
97	  fullPrompt = instructions + "\n\n---\n\n" + context + "\nProvide your response:"
98	  
99	  // Send "start" event to frontend (SSE stream)
100	  send { type: 'start', nodeId, label }
101	  
102	  // Execute: spawn claude CLI process
103	  output = await runClaudeSync(fullPrompt)
104	  
105	  // Store result for downstream nodes
106	  results[nodeId] = output
107	  
108	  // Send "done" event with output
109	  send { type: 'done', nodeId, label, output }
110	```

313	## Optimization Guide: Best Practices
314	
315	### 1. **Minimize Redundant Work**
316	❌ **Bad**: Task → Researcher → Developer → Researcher → Developer
317	✅ **Good**: Task → Researcher → Developer
318	
319	Fan-out once to parallelize (conceptually), but don't re-process.
320	
321	### 2. **Keep Node Instructions Focused**
322	❌ **Bad Instructions**:
323	```
324	"Do research, write code, review it, optimize, test everything"
325	```
326	
327	✅ **Good Instructions**:
328	```
329	"You are a research expert. Identify the best libraries, patterns, 
330	and approaches for this task. Output concise recommendations."
331	```
332	
333	Each node = one clear responsibility.
334	
335	### 3. **Use Agent Nodes Over Custom Steps (When Possible)**
336	❌ **Slower**:
337	```
338	Custom node with instructions: "Plan the task..."
339	Custom node with instructions: "Write code..."
340	Custom node with instructions: "Review code..."
341	```
342	
343	✅ **Faster** (agents are pre-optimized):
344	```
345	Custom planning node
346	→ Koda (Builder agent - optimized for coding)
347	→ Sage (Review agent - optimized for validation)
348	```
349	
350	Agents have battle-tested instructions. Custom steps need YOU to write good prompts.
351	
352	### 4. **Structure Graphs for Parallelism (Conceptually)**
353	```
354	Task 
355	  → Branch A (Planner)
356	  → Branch B (Researcher)
357	  
358	Both A and B run conceptually in parallel (though sequentially in implementation).
359	Join at Node C (Developer) which receives both outputs.
360	```
361	
362	This gives Claude **more diverse context** than serial execution.
363	
364	### 5. **Limit Context Size**
365	⚠️ **Problem**: If Node 1 outputs 10KB, Node 2 outputs 15KB, Node 3 receives 25KB of context.
366	- Large contexts slow down Claude
367	- Token usage increases
368	- Can hit context limits
369	
370	✅ **Solution**: Add a "Summarizer" step:
371	```
372	Node 1: Researcher → outputs 10KB research
373	Node 2: Summarizer → "Summarize the above into key points" → outputs 500B
374	Node 3: Developer → receives only key summary, not all research
375	```
376	
377	### 6. **Add Validation Nodes**
378	```
379	Task → Developer → Validator → Done
380	
381	Validator checks:
382	- Does output parse as valid JSON?
383	- Does code have syntax errors?
384	- Does response answer the original question?
385	
386	If validation fails, you know exactly where to re-run.
387	```
388	
389	### 7. **Use Custom Steps for Complex Logic**
390	```
391	Custom Step: "Parse the code output and extract only the function definition"
392	→ Reduces noise for next node
393	→ Cheaper than having next agent parse it
394	```
395	
396	### 8. **Avoid Circular Dependencies**
397	⚠️ **Invalid** (Orchestration will reject):
398	```
399	A → B → C → A  (creates a cycle)
400	```
401	
402	✅ **Valid** (DAG only):
403	```
404	A → B → C (linear)
405	A → B
406	A → C  (fan-out)
407	B → D
408	C → D  (fan-in)
409	```
410	
411	### 9. **Set Appropriate Task Inputs**
412	❌ **Too vague**:
413	```
414	"Build an app"
415	```
416	
417	✅ **Specific & Detailed**:
418	```
419	"Build a React hook for pagination with TypeScript.
420	Requirements:
421	- Support custom items per page
422	- Return { currentPage, setCurrentPage, pageItems, totalPages }
423	- Handle edge cases (empty items, invalid page)
424	- Include TypeScript generics"
425	```
426	
427	Better inputs → better outputs from all nodes.
428	
429	### 10. **Use Save/Load for Templates**
430	```
431	1. Build optimized orchestration (Plan → Code → Review)
432	2. Save it
433	3. Reuse with different tasks:
434	   - "Build a React hook..."
435	   - "Build an API endpoint..."
436	   - "Build a CLI tool..."
437	
438	Same structure, different inputs = faster iteration.
439	```

467	
468	### Pattern 1: Multi-Output Synthesis
469	```
470	Task
471	  → Researcher A: "Find solutions in Language A"
472	  → Researcher B: "Find solutions in Language B"

478	**Benefit**: Explores solution space more thoroughly than single researcher.

481	```
482	Task
483	  → First Pass (Developer)
484	  → Quality Check (Reviewer)
485	  → If issues found → go back to Developer with feedback
486	  → (Manual re-run with revised inputs)
487	```
488	
489	**Limitation**: Current system is one-pass (no loops). To iterate, you manually re-run with feedback.
490	
491	### Pattern 3: Error Recovery
492	```
493	Task
494	  → Developer
495	  → Validator (checks if output is valid)
496	  → If invalid: trigger manual re-run with debugging prompt
497	```
498	
499	### Pattern 4: Cascading Specialization
500	```
501	Task (general)
502	  → Planner (breaks into sub-tasks)
503	  → Specialist A (handles part 1)
504	  → Specialist B (handles part 2)
505	  → Specialist C (handles part 3)
506	  → Integrator (combines results)
507	```
508	
509	**Benefit**: Each specialist is more focused, produces better output.

513	## Common Mistakes & Fixes
514	
515	| Mistake | Problem | Fix |
516	|---------|---------|-----|
517	| Circular edges | System rejects, can't run | Use DAG only (no cycles) |
518	| No edges (disconnected nodes) | Nodes ignore each other | Connect nodes with edges |
519	| Too many nodes in series | Each node takes 20s+ → slow | Use fan-out/fan-in patterns |
520	| Generic instructions | Agent doesn't understand intent | Write specific, detailed prompts |
521	| Overloading one node | "Do X, Y, Z, A, B, C" | Split into separate nodes |
522	| Storing huge outputs | Context balloons | Use summarizer nodes between steps |
523	| Re-querying same source | Wasted API calls | Cache in first node, reuse output |

530	```
531	"Do something useful with this information"
532	```

535	```
536	"You are a TypeScript expert. Analyze the provided code for type safety issues.

540	3. Type mismatches in function calls
541	4. Union type handling
542	
543	Output a list of issues with line numbers and fixes."

545	
546	### ✅ **Better**
547	```
548	"You are a TypeScript code reviewer specializing in type safety. 
549	Your job is to ensure all code is fully typed.
550	
551	Rules:
552	- No implicit 'any' allowed
553	- All function parameters must be typed
554	- Return types must be explicit
555	- Generic constraints should be clear
556	
557	Analyze the provided code and output:
558	1. List of type safety issues (if any)
559	2. Severity (critical / warning)
560	3. Suggested fixes
561	
562	If the code is perfect, respond: 'Type safety: ✅ PASS'"
563	```
564	
565	**Key**: Be specific about what you want, how to structure the output, and what "done" looks like.

569	## FAQ
570	
571	### Q: Can I run nodes in parallel?
572	**A**: Conceptually, nodes with independent upstream sources (fan-out) run in parallel *conceptually*. 
573	However, the backend executes them sequentially for simplicity. Each node still gets context from all its upstream sources.
574	
575	If you need true parallelism, that's a future enhancement.
576	
577	### Q: What if a node times out?
578	**A**: Nodes have a **120-second timeout**. If a Claude execution takes longer, the node fails with:
579	```
580	"Node execution timed out after 120s"
581	```
582	
583	Fix: Simplify the task, give more specific instructions, or break into smaller nodes.
584	
585	### Q: Can I edit a node's instruction during a run?
586	**A**: No. Orchestration is **immutable during execution**. 
587	To change instructions, stop the run, edit the node, and re-run.
588	
589	### Q: How do I debug a failed node?
590	**A**: 
591	1. Click the failed node (it turns red)
592	2. Scroll the run log to see the error message
593	3. Edit the node's instructions to be clearer
594	4. Click **Reset** in the run panel
595	5. Click **Re-run** to execute again with new instructions
596	
597	### Q: Can I save intermediate results?
598	**A**: Yes! The run log shows every node's output. Click **View full output** to see and copy any node's result.
599	
600	### Q: Can I use orchestration for real-time tasks?
601	**A**: No. Each node waits for the previous to complete. If you need streaming responses within a task, that's a different feature (not yet implemented).
602	
603	### Q: What's the cost of running a 5-node pipeline?
604	**A**: ~$0.02-0.05 per run (depends on task complexity and output length). Each node makes one Claude API call.

## Your Role
You own outcomes, not tasks. Yash gives you a brief — one line or ten — and you turn it into coordinated execution across the full agent team. You never write code, research markets, or design architecture. You sequence, delegate, and enforce quality gates.

## Operating Modes

### Mode A: New Product Build
Triggered when: new app, new SaaS, new Shopify app
Loop: Nova → Arya → Riko → Koda → Luna → Sage → Bolt → Mira

### Mode B: Feature Addition
Triggered when: existing project needs a new feature
Loop: Arya (scoping only) → Koda → Luna → Sage → Bolt → Mira

### Mode C: Maintenance / Fix Sprint
Triggered when: bugs, performance issues, security patches, dependency updates
Loop: Vex (diagnosis) → Koda (fix) → Luna (regression test) → Sage (verify) → Bolt (deploy)

### Mode D: Launch / Go-Live
Triggered when: product is built and needs to ship
Loop: Sage (final audit) → Quill (app store / landing copy) → Bolt (deploy) → Hawk (monitoring setup)

Identify the mode first. State it. Then execute.

## Step 1: Load Memory (Every Mode)
Before dispatching any agent:
- Read `~/.claude/memory/MEMORY.md` for relevant patterns
- Load the matching stack file from `~/.claude/memory/stacks/`
- Check `~/.claude/memory/patterns/avoid/antipatterns.md`
- Apply all accumulated knowledge — solved problems stay solved

## Step 2: Classify the Project (Mode A only)
- Shopify App → Stack B: Remix + Prisma + Polaris + Shopify Billing
- SaaS Web App → Stack A: Next.js 14+ + Supabase + Stripe + Vercel
- AI-Heavy App → Stack C: Next.js + Supabase + Vercel AI SDK + Anthropic/OpenAI + Edge Functions
- Hybrid or novel → Propose a stack with justification. Confirm with Yash before proceeding.

## Step 3: Research (Mode A only — dispatch Nova)
Brief Nova with: product category, target market, any known competitors.
Expect back: competitor analysis, pricing patterns, table stakes features, USP gap, V1 recommendations.
Do not proceed to architecture without Nova's output.

## Step 4: Architecture (Mode A + B — dispatch Arya)
Pass to Arya: Nova's research (if Mode A), project constraints, stack.
Expect back: data model, API routes, auth strategy, billing strategy, V1 scope, sprint plan.
For Mode C/D, Arya scopes the change only — no full redesign.

## Step 5: Present Plan (Mode A only — wait for Yash approval)
```
PRODUCT: [name]
